IEEPA (50 U.S.C. 1701 et seq.), on which the order rests, and the order's own text contain no end; no held instrument revokes, supersedes or amends this order.
clauses.reason: Section 9 authorizes the Secretary of the Treasury to submit the recurring and final reports to Congress on the emergency under section 401(c) of the National Emergencies Act and section 204(c) of IEEPA; it is a standing authorization, not a dated deadline. On 2026-10-14 it remains in force: the emergency it implements was continued through the March 24, 2026 notice, the order's text sets no end, and no held later instrument ends it. The order's own text sets no sunset, expiry or terminating condition; section 1(b) only says the prohibitions apply notwithstanding earlier contracts, licenses or permits. The held Federal Register notices of continuation (80 FR 18081, 81 FR 19019, 82 FR 15107, 83 FR 13373, 84 FR 12871, 85 FR 18855, 86 FR 16665, 87 FR 18965, 88 FR 19211, 89 FR 21429, 90 FR 14329 and 91 FR 15513) are later events that continue the emergency and do not amend, narrow or end any clause. No held later instrument revokes, supersedes or amends this order.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 13664 of April 3, 2014 (79 FR 19283), Blocking Property of Certain Persons With Respect to South Sudan, is held in the Federal Register print (FR Doc. 2014-07895) and was read in full: a declaration of national emergency under IEEPA and the National Emergencies Act followed by ten sections. The 22-clause inventory (the opening declaration, sections 1 to 10 and their lettered or numbered paragraphs) matches the printed text. The order has no sunset or terminating condition of its own. A sentence-by-sentence search of the 31 held texts that print the number 13664 (the Federal Register print, annual continuation notices, OFAC designation notices and 31 CFR text) for revocation, supersession, rescission, termination, amendment or repeal language next to the number found none. The Federal Register catalog search returned one hit, a cross-reference in the Notice of March 24, 2026 (91 FR 15513). The other general instrument in the packet, Executive Order 14294 of May 9, 2025 (Fighting Overcriminalization in Federal Regulations), does not print this number and states a prosecution policy for criminal regulatory offenses, which gives no reason to treat any clause as extinguished. Because the order depends on a declared emergency, the twelve annual continuation notices of 2015 to 2026 are attached to every clause; the last, signed March 24, 2026, continues the emergency beyond April 3, 2026, which covers 2026-10-14. All clauses are operative on that date.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"No earlier end exists for any clause. The order contains no date, duration, condition or performance trigger that could end a clause. The held later instruments are the twelve annual continuation notices, each of which continues the emergency, and no held instrument revokes, supersedes or amends the order. The Notice of March 24, 2026 itself acts under section 202(d) of the National Emergencies Act (50 U.S.C. 1622(d)) and describes the emergency as declared under IEEPA, so the two principal authorities were still operating in 2026; nothing held shows that any authority cited in the order expired or was repealed.","independent_command_check":"The order is one blocking command with supporting prohibitions, an entry suspension, definitions, delegation and a reporting authorization. None is a one-time command that was performed and exhausted: section 4 suspends entry of an open class; section 9 authorizes recurring reports and sets no deadline. No clause is independent of the declared emergency, and no clause survives while the emergency lapses, so one continuing predicate supports all of them.","savings_check":"Savings were examined in the held text of the order and in the held later instruments. The order contains no savings or transition provision and no held instrument ends it, so no accrued right or transferred function arises.","scope_check":"Each of the 22 clauses was decided separately. Every clause is operative on the order's own held text, which has no end, read with the twelve held continuation notices and the bounded searches. The packet's current-law leads are two sections of the OFAC South Sudan regulations (31 CFR 558.106 and 558.201, eCFR amended through 2026-11-06) that restate the delegation and the blocking command; their source bytes are not held, so no clause cites them. The definitions in section 6 and the findings in sections 2, 4 and 7 operate only with the blocking command and remain with it."}

savings.reason: The order has no savings or transition clause, and none is needed because it was not revoked, superseded or ended. The held later items for this order are the continuation notices, the packet's CFR leads and OFAC notices that apply it; none ends the order or leaves a residue to preserve.
